messages.content: Find an Italian restaurant near me in New York that provides vegetarian food options and a Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

message.reasoning:
The user wants two results:

1) An Italian restaurant near them (the user says "near me") in New York that has vegetarian options.

2) A Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

We need to use the `restaurant_finder` tool twice with appropriate parameters.

First call: location="New York, NY", cuisine="Italian", preferences=["Vegetarian"] or maybe include Delivery? The requirement only mentions vegetarian options; but we can just set preferences ["Vegetarian"]. But the tool's defaults are ['Delivery']. If we want vegetarian only, we pass preferences as array containing "Vegetarian". That will override default? It might still add Delivery automatically if not specified? Not sure. We'll specify both Vegetarian and Delivery perhaps. But the request didn't ask for delivery for first one. So we could just provide Vegetarian. Let's do preferences:["Vegetarian"].

Second call: location="Los Angeles, CA", cuisine="Japanese", preferences=["Sushi"? Actually preference list includes "Delivery" so we should include it. Also maybe "Takeout" but they specifically mention delivery. So preferences:["Delivery"].

But also we may want Sushi subcategory? The tool expects cuisine like "Japanese". That's fine.

Let's produce calls accordingly.

We'll output JSON calls using the format described earlier.
